Living in Totterdown

Updated 2 November 2026. Every figure links to its source. Prices and ratings change, so check the source before you decide. How we check facts.

Totterdown is a neighbourhood of Victorian terraces on a steep hill in south Bristol, mostly in the BS4 postcode with some streets in BS3, a short walk from Temple Meads station. This guide covers the practical side of living here.

Quick answer

  • House prices: homes in Totterdown sold for an average of £374,399 over the year to early 2026, 5% more than the year before. [1]
  • Renting: example listings in 2026 asked about £1,100 a month for a one-bed flat and £1,500 for a two-bed; there's no published average for Totterdown. [2] [3]
  • Council ward: Totterdown is in Windmill Hill ward, home to an estimated 14,104 people in mid-2024. [4] [5]
  • Getting about: Temple Meads station is at the foot of the hill, within walking distance. [6]
  • Parking: a residents' parking scheme is proposed; the council's survey closes on 5 November 2026. Details
  • Clean Air Zone: Totterdown is outside Bristol's zone, which starts at the Three Lamps junction. [7]

How much are houses in Totterdown?

MeasureFigure
Average sold price, last 12 months£374,399
Change on previous year+5%
2023 peak average£365,128

Most homes in Totterdown are terraced houses, so the average reflects a mix of terrace sizes. Check recent sales on your street before making an offer. [1]

How much does it cost to rent in Totterdown?

No organisation publishes an average rent for Totterdown alone. As examples, a one-bed flat was listed at £1,100 a month and a two-bed flat at £1,500 a month in 2026. [2] [3] Compare several current listings before you agree a rent.

Where is Totterdown, and which ward is it in?

  • Location: south of the River Avon, above Temple Meads, where the A4 Bath Road and the A37 Wells Road split at Three Lamps. [8]
  • Postcodes and boundary: Totterdown has no official boundary. The residents' association TRESA notes that postcode, ward and parish boundaries all differ, and addresses fall in both BS3 and BS4. [9]
  • Ward: since 2016, Totterdown has been part of Windmill Hill ward, with the south-eastern part of Bedminster and the Ravenhill Road area of Lower Knowle. [4]
  • Population: the ward had 13,958 residents at the 2021 Census and an estimated 14,104 in mid-2024. Neither figure is for Totterdown alone. [10] [5]

What schools are in Totterdown?

Hillcrest Primary School on Cemetery Road is Totterdown's own primary school, rated Good at its January 2022 inspection. [18] There's no secondary school in Totterdown. See schools in and near Totterdown for primary and secondary options and how places are given.

How do you get around from Totterdown?

  • Train: Bristol Temple Meads is at the bottom of the hill. Visit Bristol's walking route from the station runs through Totterdown's colourful streets and over the New Cut. [6]
  • Bus: the 512 runs from Totterdown via Windmill Hill, Bedminster and Redcliffe to the city centre. Check the current timetable before you travel. [19]
  • Roads: the A4 Bath Road and the A37 Wells Road meet at Three Lamps, at the edge of Totterdown. [8]
  • Hills: many streets are steep. Vale Street has an average gradient of about 21.8%. [20]

More in getting to and around Totterdown.

Is Totterdown a safe place to live?

No source publishes a crime rate for Totterdown as a whole. For one example, StreetCheck counted 57 crimes within half a mile of Bath Road, Totterdown, in October 2025 and rated the level "medium". [21] For a street you're thinking of moving to, look up its postcode on the police.uk crime map, which shows recorded crime month by month. [22]

Is Totterdown in the Clean Air Zone?

No. Bristol's Clean Air Zone has been running since 28 November 2022. [23] Totterdown sits just outside it: the boundary starts at the Three Lamps junction, so drivers coming in on the Bath Road can turn onto the Wells Road without entering the zone. [7]

  • Charge: £9 a day for non-compliant private cars; fully electric vehicles don't pay. [23]
  • Possible rise: the council has considered raising some charges to £14 a day. [24] Check the council's checker before you drive in.

What is changing near Totterdown?

  • Residents' parking and Liveable Neighbourhood: both are being consulted on or designed now. Read the guide.
  • Temple Island: Bristol City Council approved Legal & General's £350m Temple Island scheme, with 520 homes, offices, a hotel and shops, in April 2026. [25] Objectors argued the towers would block views of Totterdown's coloured houses from the city. [26]

Community groups

  • TRESA (Totterdown Residents' Environmental and Social Action) holds public meetings on planning, transport and local issues. [27]
  • Arts trail: the Totterdown Arts Trail opens homes to visitors every November.
  • Events: see what's on in Totterdown through the year.
